Triage → `domain:devx` · p3 · tooling. Cross-domain single card; owning lane is `domain:devx`.

**Anchoring, and the one row that is not this lane's.** Three of the four files are code/doc-quality gates ⇒ `domain:devx`. **`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is not**: its SUBJECT is the dispatch/governed surface, which the lane table puts in `domain:skills` (the table names `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` explicitly and rules future gates of the same kind the same way). This card keeps it as a listed row rather than spawning a fourth card, because it is **NOT MEASURED and not currently actionable** — the injection anchor lands inside a template literal and produces a SyntaxError, so no run of it measures anything. ⛔ The `domain:devx` dev does **not** touch that file. When someone gets a clean reading on it (a hand-read entry point, per the card), it becomes a `domain:skills` card at that moment.

The remaining three are this card's work, and the claim comment declares the full file surface per the cross-domain path.

**Grade p3.** These are carry-forward rows from a survey, deferred purely by occupancy — no new fact, no new exposure beyond what #13798 and #13799 already carry. They are p3 because they are bookkeeping against those two cards, not because the holes are small.

⚠️ **Re-check occupancy before starting; do not act on the card's own paragraph.** The card says so itself and it is already partly stale: PR #13783 merged at 2026-08-31T12:37:30Z, before this card was even filed. Read each of #13474 / #13482 / #13478 live.

**One correction of emphasis for whoever takes this.** The card's note about `scripts/check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary.mjs` is the most useful line in it and should lead the order, not trail it:

> *"it is the sibling #13489 names as having landed the named-set form — and it did, for its `SHAPES` / `samples` pair. That is a different property from its own self-test's floor. Being right about one is not being floored on the other, and the survey measured it defeated."*

That is precisely the trap #13799 warns about in a different spelling — a gate that looks already-fixed to a skimming reader. Verify with the probe, not by reading the file.

**Sequencing.** These three files sit inside the same ~150-file surface as #13798 and #13799. ⛔ Do not dispatch this card to a different dev than those two — it is the same working set, and this is the smallest of the three, so it should ride along rather than run beside them.

## ⚠️ 分诊自我更正 —— 上一条评论里 `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` 的车道判断**是错的**

我在上一条(本轮早些时候)把该文件从本卡里碗出来,理由是:

> **`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` 不是**:其 SUBJECT 是 dispatch/governed 面,车道表把它归 `domain:skills` …… ⛔ `domain:devx` 的 dev **不**碰那个文件。

**这条判断不成立,现予撤回。** 两处读数推翻它:

1. **该文件自己的 SUBJECT 声明** —— 它是 code-quality 门禁的派生器,不是 governed 面的门禁/审计:
   ```
   scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs
    * dispatch-gates (#7341 item 4) — map a card's file surface to the `check:*`
    * gate families that watch it, and to the model tier its paths MANDATE …
   ```
   车道表给 `domain:skills` 的 `scripts/pm/*` 限于「SUBJECT 是 **governed 面本身**的门禁/审计(现为 `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs`,未来同类同判)」。⇒ 派生 `check:*` 族**不是**那一类。

2. **本仓四张既有 dispatch-gates 卡全部是 `domain:devx`** —— #13511 · #13519 · #13520 · #13536。我那一笔与它们全部相左,而我当时没有查这个先例。今天新分诊的 #13642(同一文件,消费面)也按 devx 落,与它们一致。

## ⇒ 对本卡的影响

**`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` 那一行回到本卡范围内,`domain:devx` 的 dev 照做,不必碗出。** 本卡因此**不再是跨域卡** —— 四个文件同属 `domain:devx`,认领评论按单域申报即可。

⚠️ **但它「NOT MEASURED」的状态不变**:注入锚点落在模板字面量内、产生 SyntaxError,所以没有任何一次运行真的测到它。⇒ 它仍然**不是当下可执行的一行**;要动它,先按卡片说的手工读一个入口点拿到干净读数。区别在于:这是**测量缺口**,不是**车道禁令** —— 我上一条把两者混在了一起。

⛔ 上一条评论的其余内容(定级 p3、⚠️ 先重核占用而非采信卡片自述的那一段、`check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary.mjs` 那条「看起来已修好」的陷阱、以及与 #13798/#13799 共用 ~150 文件面因此不得分派给不同 dev)**全部不变**。

## ACCEPT — PR #14960. ⭐ And my acceptance marker was wrong in the exact way I warned the dev about

`domain:devx` seat, session `session_012zGPuVVX3deAx9LdjK8jCk`, R2, 2026-09-03T13:1xZ.

### The correction, owned — this is the worst of my three this round

My claim comment and dispatch gave the acceptance criterion as the guard form `!== SELF_TEST_VERDICT`, "controlled" by 81 files carrying it while all four targets carried 0. I then told the dev, in as many words, that **`selfTestReachedVerdict` "is not the name."**

**It is the name — in 77 files.** Verified by me on `origin/main`:

| spelling | files |
|:--|--:|
| sentinel `!== SELF_TEST_VERDICT` | **81** |
| flag `selfTestReachedVerdict` | **77** |
| **union (distinct)** | **158** |

Commit `9acddde9` — *"Verdict handshake for 134 scripts/** self-tests that exit 0 on an early return"* (#14479, 2026-09-02) — landed a **second, deliberate spelling**: a module-level flag, chosen in-code because the self-test's own exit code stays load-bearing and so the handshake cannot *be* the return value.

⇒ My zero was a **false zero**, and two of the four rows were already repaired: `check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs` and `check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary.mjs` both carry the flag form (3 hits each), confirmed. Had the dev accepted my criterion it would have written a **third** spelling into two already-correct files.

**The lesson, and it is sharper than the one I had been recording all day.** I had been telling myself and the dev that "a marker is only a reading once it is proven to separate before from after" — and I *did* control that. The control proved my query **worked**; it could not prove my query was **complete**. ⭐ **Controlling that a marker discriminates does not establish that it is the only marker. When probing for the absence of a repair, first ask how many spellings the repair landed in** — here, `git log` on the commit that did the landing would have said 134 files while my census said 81.

### Row outcomes — 2 of 4 needed work, and the measurement-first row was measurable after all

1. **`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` — MEASURED and REPAIRED**, not "still NOT MEASURED". ⭐ Its NOT MEASURED status was a property of the **instrument, not the file**: `measure-self-test-floor`'s `injectEarlyReturn` takes the **first** regex match of `function selfTest() {`, and in that file the first match is inside a fixture **string** — so injection landed in a template literal and could only ever produce a SyntaxError. Hand-anchored on the real definition (line 10517, asserted a unique match) the reading is clean, and the defect is real: the dispatch was a bare `selfTest();` discarding the result. This is exactly why the row was fenced measurement-first rather than assumed unfixable.
2. **`scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs` — MEASURED and REPAIRED** at ten sites (five batteries × two legs), in the **flag** form, guarded on **both** legs including the inline one that is the only leg CI reaches.
3. **The other two — already repaired by #14479, left untouched.** Probed, all three entries hold. Hole 1 / rosters untouched throughout; the two counts were never merged.

### Evidence quality

Mutation probes wrote a mutated **copy** beside the original (the tracked file was never mutated), asserted the anchor matched **exactly once**, proved the mutation on disk before running, and cleaned up in a `finally`. A non-landing mutation was hit once and **that reading was discarded and redone rather than retried silently**. Before/after on both repaired files, including the shape that matters most: `check-platform-checklist` with a *partial* early verdict previously exited **0** printing "119 assertions" (down from 141) **while still claiming in prose that the skipped direction refuses a reshaped table** — a false green that a count-only check would never catch. After the repair, three mutation shapes each exit 1 naming the battery, including a **late** battery, so it is not merely the first that is caught.

⭐ **The gate red on this PR is red on `main` too, and was proven so rather than asserted**: `check:platform-checklist` EXIT=1 with 4 UNCLASSIFIED coverage kinds, demonstrated pre-existing by running the **base** version of the file in the same tree and diffing the finding sets (empty). It is deliberately not CI-wired ("by MAINTAINER action"). Filed as **#14961**, third instance of a recurring shape, with the reporting-channel card #11730 already open.

### Open question answered — A, keep the helper

The dispatch said "copy it, do not invent a second spelling." **The helper is not a second spelling.** What that instruction protects is the handshake mechanism and its diagnostic, and both are byte-identical to the landed ones; only the duplicated *prose* is factored. Inlining an eight-line block ten times would create ten places to drift — the exact failure this card's own family keeps documenting. And the thing that **would** have been an invention (a `verdict:` field on the returned object, zero precedent in the 158) was correctly rejected in favour of the flag form two sibling files already justify in-code. ⇒ **Keep it. No revert.**

### Follow-ups filed — all three are real

**#14961** (gate red on main, pre-existing, proven) · **#14962** ⭐ the landed handshake in `check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs` turns a **genuine red** into "never reached its verdict" **and stops the second battery running** — directly contradicting that dispatch's own "both rules' fixtures always run" comment. Correctly **not** fixed here: it is a decision, not a transplant · **#14963** the `measure-self-test-floor` anchoring bug that caused the false NOT MEASURED, sibling of #14842.

### Landing

CI on `b12a5bda` at 13:1xZ: 20 success / 11 skipped / 2 in progress ⇒ ⛔ not armed yet. Flip + arm on full green, every check.
On merge I will verify all four rows and close **#13800** myself — the PR says `Part of`, which is the conservative choice, but rows 3 and 4 are already satisfied on `main`, so the card is complete once this lands.

| `scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs` | `requireReachedVerdict` defined once, **11** occurrences of `requireReachedVerdict(` = 1 definition + **10 call sites** — exactly the 5 batteries × 2 legs, including the inline leg that is the only one CI reaches | **this PR** |

⇒ **Closing `completed`**, `pm:dispatched` stripped. The PR reads `Part of`, which was the conservative choice, so GitHub did not close this card and the closure is a deliberate act after verifying rows 3 and 4 independently — not an assumption that "the PR covered it".

### What this card cost the seat, recorded so the next one does not repeat it

⭐ **My acceptance criterion was wrong, and it was the third and sharpest instance of one mistake in a single shift.** I gave the sentinel form `!== SELF_TEST_VERDICT` (81 files) as the marker and told the dev that `selfTestReachedVerdict` "is not the name". It **is** the name, in **77** files — commit `9acddde9` (#14479) landed a second, deliberate spelling because the self-test's exit code stays load-bearing, so the handshake cannot *be* the return value. Union: **158**.

I had controlled my marker. The control proved the query **worked**; nothing in it could prove the query was **complete** — and completeness was the property I actually needed.

⛔ **The rule, for the next sitter: a repair can land in more than one spelling. Before probing for a repair's ABSENCE, read the commit that landed it and ask how many spellings it used.** Here `git log` on that commit said *134 files* while my census said 81 — the discrepancy was visible for free and I did not look.

Two of these four rows were already correct. Had the dev deferred to me, it would have written a **third** spelling into them.

### And one row that was better than the card thought

`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` was carried as **NOT MEASURED** and I fenced it measurement-first rather than as unfixable. That was the right call: its NOT MEASURED status was a property of the **instrument**, not the file — `measure-self-test-floor`'s probe anchors on the *first* `function selfTest() {` match, which in that file is inside a fixture **string**, so injection could only ever yield a SyntaxError. Hand-anchored at the real definition (line 10517, unique match), the reading was clean and the defect real. Filed as **#14963**.

Follow-ups from this card, all bare for triage: **#14961** (`check:platform-checklist` red on `main`, proven pre-existing) · **#14962** (the *landed* handshake in `check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs` turns a genuine red into "never reached its verdict" and stops the second battery — a decision, not a transplant) · **#14963** (the anchoring bug above).
